```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5, dpi = 150)
project.folder <- paste0(here::here(), "/")
source(paste0(project.folder, "create_folder_structure.R"))
source(paste0(functions.folder, "script_initiate.R"))
suppressMessages({library(INLA); library(Matrix); library(viridisLite)})
INLA::inla.setOption(num.threads = 2)
source(paste0(functions.folder, "inla_dlnm_helpers.R"))

PREC <- 4; NS2 <- list(fun = "ns", df = 2); LIN <- list(fun = "lin")
PANEL_ORD <- c("Minnesota", "Other flyway states", "Pooled")
OK  <- setNames(viridisLite::viridis(3, begin = 0.05, end = 0.78), PANEL_ORD)
SHP <- setNames(c(16, 17, 15), PANEL_ORD)
lab_num <- scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
LABEL <- c(temperature = "Temperature", precipitation = "Precipitation",
           soil_moisture = "Soil moisture", wind_speed = "Wind speed",
           anseriformes = "Anseriformes")
```

## SF2. Deviation from the 25-year climatological normal

Figure 3's layout for the third exposure parameterisation. Figure 3 shows absolute conditions and
the 90-day departure; this is the same model fitted to each day's deviation from the 1997–2021
weekly normal for that cell — the parameterisation a reader most naturally means by "anomaly".

```{r sf2-clim}
# This panel needs no 90-day warm-up, so it keeps 175 cases against the 167 in Figure 3. The
# extra 8 are all outside Minnesota.
D <- setDT(readRDS(paste0(objects_folder, "case_crossover_df_climanom_post7.RDS")))
if (anyDuplicated(names(D))) D <- D[, which(!duplicated(names(D))), with = FALSE]
CLIM <- paste0(c("temperature", "precipitation", "soil_moisture", "wind_speed"), "_clim")
have <- CLIM[vapply(CLIM, function(v) paste0(v, "_Lag0") %in% names(D), TRUE)]

panel_of <- function(pn) {
  if (pn == "Minnesota") D[state == "Minnesota"]
  else if (pn == "Pooled") copy(D) else D[state != "Minnesota"]
}
clim <- rbindlist(lapply(PANEL_ORD, function(pn) {
  d  <- panel_of(pn)
  mv <- c(have, "anseriformes")
  av <- c(setNames(rep(list(NS2), length(have)), have), list(anseriformes = LIN))
  o  <- assemble_cc_dlnm(d, met_vars = mv, weekly_vars = character(0), max_lag = 28,
                         argvar_by_var = av, arglag = list(fun = "ns", df = 2))
  f  <- suppressWarnings(fit_cc_inla_dlnm(o, fixed_prec = PREC))
  rbindlist(lapply(mv, function(v) rbindlist(lapply(names(INLA_LAG_WINDOWS), function(k) {
    w <- INLA_LAG_WINDOWS[[k]]
    e <- met_lag_effect(f, o, v, seq(w[1], w[2]))
    data.table(panel = pn, n = sum(d$outbreak_binary),
               variable = unname(LABEL[sub("_clim$", "", v)]), window = k,
               RR = e[["OR"]], low = e[["low"]], high = e[["high"]])
  }))))
}))
clim[, `:=`(panel = factor(panel, levels = PANEL_ORD),
            window = factor(window, levels = names(INLA_LAG_WINDOWS)),
            variable = factor(variable, levels = rev(c("Temperature", "Precipitation",
                                                       "Soil moisture", "Wind speed",
                                                       "Anseriformes"))))]
saveRDS(clim, paste0(objects_folder, "sf2_climatological_anomaly.RDS"))

fig <- ggplot(clim, aes(RR, variable, colour = panel, shape = panel)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), height = 0, linewidth = 0.55,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.66, reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.1, position = position_dodge(width = 0.66, reverse = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~ window, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = OK) + scale_shape_manual(values = SHP) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log", breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3), labels = lab_num) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, 3.5)) +
  labs(x = "Rate ratio per +0.5 standard deviation increase in exposure",
       y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Avenir") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
        strip.text = element_text(family = "Avenir Heavy", size = 11),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4))
ggsave_spark(file.path(figures_main_folder, "figureS2_climatological_anomaly.png"),
             fig, width = 13, height = 4.5)
fig
```

```{r sf2-table}
clim[, cell := sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", RR, low, high)]
knitr::kable(dcast(clim, variable ~ panel + window, value.var = "cell"))
```
